reasons: Only the first two sections are visible, so the rest of the file cannot be judged.

terms.meaning: Code that turns stored data into the shape the app shows.

sections.name: File setup, MISSING_FIELDS_LIST, ZERO_VALID
sections.title: Imports and required field lists
sections.what: Brings in helpers and types, then lists ten fields that count toward completeness. Also lists delay months as a field where zero is allowed.
sections.why: The names show the purpose: a fixed list of fields to check, and an exception for a real zero.
sections.watch_out: Zero is treated as missing for every field except delay months.

sections.name: computeMissing
sections.title: Counting missing key fields
sections.what: Checks each listed field. Records the field if it is empty, or if it is zero and zero is not allowed. Returns the count and the names.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the list show how complete each project record is.
sections.watch_out: Only fields in the fixed list are checked, so a new field must be added there to count.

sections.name: ProjectListRow
sections.title: Shape of a project list row
sections.what: Defines the fields each project carries in the project list, such as name, budget, dates, status, location, cost deviation and missing-data counts. Many values can be empty.
sections.why: Gives the list screens one fixed row format.
sections.watch_out: Many fields can be null, so any screen reading them must handle empty values.

sections.name: toProjectListRow
sections.title: Turns a project into a list row
sections.what: Converts a stored project into a list row. It counts missing core fields, calculates the cost deviation percentage rounded to one decimal, and attaches short evidence only when it is requested.
sections.why: Likely reason: the list needs a small, consistent row rather than the full project record.
sections.watch_out: This builder uses the stored industry as is, while the detail builder defaults it to nuclear, so the two views can disagree on a record with no industry.

summary: Prepares the short summary row for one project in the project list, including which key fields are missing.
purpose: Lets the project list show each project briefly, with a count of missing information so a user can see which records need work.
why: Reason not stated in the code as a whole. The visible part defines which fields count as missing, and the explanation for that rule is in the names.
how: 1. A fixed list names ten fields that matter for completeness. 2. A short list says delay months may be zero, because zero is a real answer there. 3. `computeMissing` checks each listed field and records any that are empty, or zero where zero is not allowed. The rest of the file, including the row shape and `toProjectListRow`, is not explained here.
inputs: A project record from the database.
outputs: A count of missing fields and their names, used in the list row.
risks: Zero counts as missing for every listed field except delay months, so a real zero budget looks missing. Adding a new field requires updating the fixed list.
debug: If a project shows the wrong missing count, compare its stored values with the fixed list. A zero that should show as missing for a field other than delay months means the rule is working as written.
